struct.name: BoardPostLengthsRecord
struct.comment: Length triple for a single board post. Read inside a chunked block — each short is followed by a 0xFF delimiter. The corresponding string bytes are stored later, after the chunked block ends.

struct.name: BoardRecord
struct.comment:
A single board section. The entire record occupies the byte span declared for this board in BoardFile.board_sizes.
On-disk layout: chunked: post_count : short, 0xFF for each post: name_length, subject_length, body_length (each short, 0xFF) end chunked for each post: name : Windows-1252 bytes, no terminator, length = name_length subject : Windows-1252 bytes, no terminator, length = subject_length body : Windows-1252 bytes, no terminator, length = body_length
Strings are concatenated back-to-back with no length prefix and no chunk delimiters between them. The reversible map/sign byte transformation used elsewhere in the EO encoding is NOT applied to these strings. Carriage returns (0x0D) inside body text are literal line breaks.
An empty board (post_count = 0) is exactly 3 bytes: 01 FE FF.

struct.name: BoardFile
struct.comment:
Endless Board File (dbbXXX.ebf). Stores all posts for the eight in-game boards on a server.
File layout: board_sizes : 8 × int (32 bytes total) — byte size of each board section boards : 8 × BoardRecord, each sized exactly board_sizes[i]
Total file size = 32 + sum(board_sizes). Boards are 1-indexed in game but stored in array order 0..7.

array.name: board_sizes
array.comment: Byte size of each of the 8 board sections that follow

array.name: boards
array.comment: The i-th board occupies exactly board_sizes[i] bytes. Readers should slice each section by its declared size before parsing, since the chunked metadata alone does not bound the trailing string data.
